To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Pla2g 6 mutation disrupts the dependency of Glutamate (Glu) induced extracellular Ca2+-influx on mitochondrial Ca2+-uptake in neurons, and that in astrocytes this Glu-induced Ca 2+-influx is reduced by ∼2-fold, but not by mitochondrial Ca2+-transport.
in neurons and astro-cytes of three INAD mouse strains with Pla2 g6 mutations, we detected characteristic changes in glutamate (G lu)-induced Ca2+ signals, but specific for each cell type.
the Pla2g 6 mutation disrupted the mitochondrial Ca2+ dependent Glu-induced Ca 2+ influx in neurons and reduced the Glu-induced capacitative Ca2 + entry in astrocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of pathways and mechanisms, which are altered in INAD, and with the understanding of non-canonical functions of PLA2G6.
the question of how the lack of PLA2G6 activity leads to disease in infantile neuroaxial dystrophy (INADS).
the elucidation of the mechanisms of the neurodegenerative infantile neuroaxional dystrophy (INaD)
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Pla2g mutation leads to a decrease in Ca2+ signaling in astrocytes and neurons.
the lack of VIA iPla2 activity in INAD mouse models leads to altered Ca2+ homeostasis in astrocytes but not in neurons.
the Pla2g mutations cause the INAD pathology by a loss of function, which is a reduction in the Ca2+ -dependent PLA2 activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in neurons with Pla 2g6 mutation the Glu-induced extracelluar Ca2+ influx is no longer dependent on mitochondrial Ca2+, and in astrocytes the Glu-induced capacitative Ca2++ influx is reduced.
INAD pathology in neurons and astroctyes is associated with alterations in Glu-evoked Ca2+ responses, and that these alterations are caused by lack of VIA iPA2 activity.
the Pla2g mutations in INAD lead to changes in Glu-evoked Ca2+ signaling in both astrocytes and neurons, which are mediated by different mechanisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pla2g 6-mutation causes a specific alteration in astrocyte Ca2+ signaling and that this may represent a key pathogenic mechanism in INAD.
the lack of PLA2G6 activity in astrocytes is sufficient to mimic the INAD pathology in these cells.
astrocytes with reduced iPLA2-activity show reduced capacitative Ca2- entry, which leads to reduced duration of Glu-induced astrocyte Ca2+ responses.
